Do not inherit median_abs_move 3.63% or up_count 3/8 as an earnings base rate.
where_to_look: Richemont's disclosures on its equity-accounted stake. Richemont took ~33-36% of LuxExperience when it sold YNAP into Mytheresa in April 2025 and equity-accounts it; the FY26 Annual Report and Accounts (year to 31 March 2026) discloses the share of associate results and flagged LuxExperience as the reason associate income fell — https://www.richemont.com/media/045hlucv/richemont-fy26-annual-report-and-accounts.pdf . That gives a third-party read on LUXE's loss run-rate through the March quarter that almost nobody covering a $1bn ADR will have pulled.

The Q3 FY26 release explicitly 'confirmed full fiscal year 2026 guidance' — https://investors.luxexperience.com/news/news-details/2026/Q3-FY26-Results-LuxExperience-Group-Reports-Positive-Adjusted-EBITDA-Profitability-for-the-Second-Consecutive-Quarter-Confirming-Full-Fiscal-Year-2026-Guidance-as-Transformation-Plan-Is-Fully-on-Track/default.aspx . The unpriced question is the FY27 guide, not the FY26 actual, since the FY26 number is guided and the consensus EPS of -$0.17 against last year's +$5.30 is a post-YNAP comparability break rather than a forecast.

YNAP integration cash cost and the restructuring provision: the separable question is how much of the announced transformation cost has actually been taken versus remains, which sits in the 20-F/6-K cash-flow detail rather than the release headline.

Option chain is unusable as a prior: ATM bid-ask is 67% of mid on 714 contracts of total open interest, so the 10.94% implied move in the baseline is indicative only and is not evidence of what the market expects.
